newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power firm ahead of cold front.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power firm ahead of cold front.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in northeastern U.S. Monday finished firm against Friday's levels ahead of the arrival of a cold front, which could unleash rain, snow and ice over parts of the region.
For Tuesday, temperatures in the Northeast were predicted to stay seasonal in 20s-40s Fahrenheit range, but temperatures were forecast to plummet 10-15 degrees below normal Wednesday.

Although coal, nuclear and hydro generation remained ample to meet current demand, the cold snap, if lengthy, could push physical prices sharply higher because utilities and other generators could be forced to switch on expensive oil and natural gas generation, marketers said.

At utility receipt points in the New York City area, swing gas values were assessed near $4.20 per million British thermal units, down from Friday's high of $4.75 in step with lower Gulf Coast prices.
December New York City gate deliveries ended today in the $4.90 area, off from $5.00 on Friday, but still up more than $1.50 from November market-related indices.
"I would expect it would have an impact on December prices, but not yet," a Northeast trader said.

In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Tuesday were notationally valued near $24.00-$25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with Friday's quotes near $24.00.

Western New York prices for Monday were pegged higher in tandem with stronger values in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool. Western New York generators had been selling power into northern PJM because of more attractive prices.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Tuesday remained in the $14.00-$15.00 range.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity was assessed for Tuesday at $28.00-$29.00, up from Friday's $27.00-$28.00.
Off-peak, non-firm power in eastern NYPP was talked for Tuesday at $17.00-$18.00, flat from Friday.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday at the Northeast Utilities border was quoted at $32.00-$33.00, up from Friday's $31.00-$32.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Tuesday delivery to the NU border held steady near $21.00.
Trading activity in the Northeast bulk power market was expected to stay light ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday weekend.

A 355 megawatt (MW) unit at the coal-fired Merrimack generating station in central New Hampshire was scheduled to to resume operation this past weekend after being shut October 25 for boiler maintenance.
